mainTopic: The dignity and definition of a תלמיד חכם, stains as a barrier in טבילה, and offering שבת fats on יום הכיפורים or יום טוב
overview: This amud is about how a תלמיד חכם should look and what makes someone a real תלמיד חכם. It opens with a source in the תורה that changing clothes shows respect: the כהן changes before taking out the ashes, which דבי רבי ישמעאל call דרך ארץ. Then רבי יוחנן teaches that patched shoes (only a patch on a patch) and stained clothes are a disgrace for a scholar, because he makes the תורה look bad. A משנה about a grease stain as a barrier in טבילה leads ריש לקיש to ask about a saddle. רבי חנינא answers from רבי יוסי, who says the clothes of בנאין count even with a stain on one side. רבי יוחנן says בנאין are תלמידי חכמים, and the גמרא adds his definitions of a scholar: one trusted to identify lost items by sight, one fit to lead, and one whose town must support him. ריש לקיש instead says בנאין are overseas bath attendants, and the גמרא settles a question about the color of their clothes. Finally, the גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל's view in the משנה: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue whether fats from שבת offerings may be burned on a following יום הכיפורים or a following יום טוב. רבי זירא's comment begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where does the תורה show that changing clothes is respectful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה that changing one's clothes is a matter of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know, from the תורה, about changing clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question and is setting up the next move. It wants a source in the תורה showing that changing into different clothes is a way of giving honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the topic was the value of special clothing. Now the גמרא wants to anchor the idea of שינוי בגדים in a פסוק instead of treating it as a mere custom.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (a request for a source)
From the תורה, from a פסוק

phrases.english: From where do we derive changing clothes from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין לְשִׁנּוּי בְּגָדִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section by asking for a תורה source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that changing clothes is a form of respect.

steps.title: The כהן changes his clothes before removing the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק about the כהן taking off his garments and putting on other garments before he carries the ashes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he shall take off his garments and put on other garments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from ויקרא. Before the כהן takes the ashes out of the camp, he takes off his clothes and puts on different ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself does not say why the כהן changes. The next step will explain that the reason is respect, so the cleaner clothes are kept for the more honored service.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
And he shall take off his garments

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And he shall take off his garments'
'and put on other garments'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:ד, about the כהן taking the ashes outside the camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּפָשַׁט אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְלָבַשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן changes his clothes before taking out the ashes, so changing clothes is found in the תורה.

steps.title: The lesson: don't serve your master in your cooking clothes
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל explain that the פסוק teaches manners: clothes worn while cooking for one's master should not be worn while pouring his drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The תורה taught proper manners. In the clothes he wore while cooking a pot for his master, he should not pour a cup for his master.
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל explains the reason behind the פסוק. The כהן changes clothes as a lesson in דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking gets clothes dirty, but serving a drink is done in front of the master and calls for clean clothes. In the same way, the כהן does the dirty job of removing ashes in different clothes from the ones he wears for the honored service. This turns the פסוק into a general lesson in respect.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: Changing clothes has a source in the תורה: the כהן changes before removing the ashes. דבי רבי ישמעאל teach that this is דרך ארץ, meaning you don't serve your master in dirty work clothes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the whole section: how a person dresses shows respect for others and for the תורה.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
The Torah taught proper manners:
Clothes in which he cooked a pot for his master
he should not pour a cup for his master in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, לִימְּדָה תּוֹרָה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of the פסוק brought in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not wear the clothes you got dirty during lowly work when doing honored service. This is דרך ארץ taught by the תורה.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם should not go to the market in patched shoes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it is disgraceful for a תלמיד חכם to go out to the market in patched shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is a disgrace for a תלמיד חכם to go out to the market in patched shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a series of teachings from רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן. This first one says a תלמיד חכם should not go out in public in patched shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theme moves from respect for one's master to the dignity of a תלמיד חכם. Because he represents the תורה, a shabby appearance in public is called a disgrace (גנאי).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is a disgrace for a Torah scholar
to go out in patched shoes to the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of respectful clothing with a new statement about a תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is disgraceful for a תלמיד חכם to go to the market in patched shoes.

steps.title: But רבי אחא בר חנינא did go out that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule: רבי אחא בר חנינא, a תלמיד חכם, went out in patched shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אחא בר חנינא went out in them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the conduct of a known scholar. רבי אחא בר חנינא went out in patched shoes, so how can it be a disgrace?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great scholar would not do something disgraceful. So his behavior suggests that patched shoes are acceptable, which seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא נָפֵיק!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Acha bar Chanina went out (in patched shoes)!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא נָפֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that patched shoes are a disgrace for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A respected scholar did exactly this, which suggests it is not disgraceful.

steps.title: Only a patch on top of a patch is a disgrace
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בריה דרב נחמן answers that the disgrace is only a patch placed over another patch. A single patch is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בריה דרב נחמן said: It refers to a patch on top of a patch.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by narrowing the rule. רבי יוחנן only meant shoes with a patch on top of a patch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single patch is normal and not shameful, and that is what רבי אחא בר חנינא wore. Layered patches look very shabby, and that is what רבי יוחנן called a disgrace. Both sources now fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: A patch on top of a patch

steps.whatToRemember: A single patch on a shoe is fine even for a תלמיד חכם. Only a patch on top of a patch is a disgrace in public.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha the son of Rav Nachman said:
(It refers to) a patch on top of a patch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: בִּטְלַאי עַל גַּב טְלַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (limiting the rule to a specific situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to cover any patched shoe, which would contradict רבי אחא בר חנינא's practice.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a patch on top of a patch is disgraceful. A single patch, as רבי אחא בר חנינא wore, is fine.

steps.title: A scholar with a stain on his clothes deserves death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a תלמיד חכם with a stain (רבב) on his clothing is 'liable to death,' based on reading the פסוק as 'those who cause Me to be hated.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any תלמיד חכם on whose garment a fat stain is found is liable to death, as it says: 'All those who hate Me love death.' Do not read 'those who hate Me' (מְשַׂנְאַי), but 'those who cause Me to be hated' (מַשְׂנִיאַי).
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement of רבי יוחנן: a תלמיד חכם who goes around with a stain on his clothes is described very harshly as חייב מיתה. He learns this from a פסוק in משלי, read in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through an אל תקרי, the word מְשַׂנְאַי ('those who hate Me') is read as מַשְׂנִיאַי ('those who make Me hated'). A sloppy scholar makes people look down on the תורה he represents. That is why the language is so strong.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to death (here a strong expression of how serious it is)
Do not read it as... (a homiletic re-reading of a word)
Those who cause Me (the Torah) to be hated

steps.confusionAlert: 'חייב מיתה' here is not a death penalty carried out by a בית דין. It is a strong way of saying how serious it is to make the תורה look bad.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Any Torah scholar on whom a fat stain is found
on his garment is liable to death,
as it says: 'All those who hate Me love death'
phrases.notes: משלי ח:לו, where the תורה (wisdom) is speaking.

phrases.english: Do not read 'those who hate Me' but 'those who cause Me to be hated.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁנִּמְצָא רְבָב עַל בִּגְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement in the same series of רבי יוחנן teachings about a scholar's appearance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם with a stain on his clothing is considered 'liable to death,' because he causes the תורה to be disrespected.

steps.title: רבינא: the word was רבד, not רבב
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports a different version of רבי יוחנן's statement: the word was רבד, a more serious stain (Sefaria, following רבינו חננאל: a bloodstain).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: 'רבד' was said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different version of the word in רבי יוחנן's statement. It was not רבב (a fat stain) but רבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word is רבד, the rule is about a more serious, more noticeable stain, not just any grease spot. This sounds like a disagreement over how strict the rule is, and the next step will deal with that.

keyTerms.meaning: A different kind of stain (per רבינו חננאל, a bloodstain)
It was said, the statement was

phrases.english: Ravina said: 'Revad' was stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: רְבָד אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of the key word in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The version of רבי יוחנן's statement reads רבד, a more serious stain, instead of רבב.

steps.title: No real dispute: outer cloak versus undergarment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two versions do not argue. One refers to an outer cloak and the other to an undergarment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: this one refers to an outer cloak, that one refers to an undergarment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two versions of the word do not really conflict. Each one is talking about a different garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On an outer cloak (גלימא), which everyone sees, even an ordinary fat stain (רבב) is disgraceful. On an undergarment (לבושא), which is less visible, only the more serious stain (רבד) is a problem. So both versions are correct, each for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... that one (splitting two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A stain on a scholar's clothes is a serious matter. On an outer garment, any stain counts. On an undergarment, only a more serious stain counts.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא בִּגְלִימָא, הָא בִּלְבוּשָׁא.
phrases.english: And they do not disagree: this is regarding an outer cloak, that is regarding an undergarment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא בִּגְלִימָא, הָא בִּלְבוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two versions from steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each version refers to a different garment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבב and רבד looked like two competing versions of one rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבב applies to an outer cloak and רבד to an undergarment, so both versions are true.

steps.title: ישעיהו's 'naked and barefoot' means worn clothes and patched shoes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that ישעיהו going 'naked and barefoot' means he wore worn-out clothes and patched shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is meant by what is written, 'As My servant ישעיהו went naked and barefoot'? 'Naked' means in worn-out clothes, and 'barefoot' means in patched shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: A third statement of רבי יוחנן explains a פסוק in ישעיהו. The prophet was not literally naked and barefoot; he wore worn-out clothes and patched shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ישעיהו's appearance as a sign of humiliation. רבי יוחנן reads it to mean shabby clothing, which the פסוק calls 'naked.' This fits the earlier steps: worn clothes and patched shoes really are seen as a disgrace for an important person.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written

steps.whatToRemember: When a פסוק calls someone 'naked' or 'barefoot,' it can mean shabby clothes and patched shoes. This shows how seriously a poor appearance was viewed for an important person.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
What is meant by what is written: 'As My servant Isaiah went'
'naked and barefoot'?
'Naked' means in worn-out clothes,
'and barefoot' means in patched shoes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement in the series. It ties back to the patched-shoes idea of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פסוק about ישעיהו, 'naked' means worn-out clothes and 'barefoot' means patched shoes.

steps.title: The משנה on a stain as a barrier in immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a grease stain on a saddle blocks the water during טבילה. On clothing, the תנאים disagree whether a stain on one side is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: A grease stain on a saddle is a barrier. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: only if it is as big as an Italian איסר. On clothing, a stain on one side is not a barrier, but a stain that goes through to both sides is a barrier. רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי ישמעאל: even one side is a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה about stains and טבילה. This continues the earlier topic of stains on clothing and sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item being immersed must have nothing blocking the water from touching it. That blocking is called חציצה. A stain on a saddle blocks the water, and the תנאים argue about how big the stain must be and whether one side of a garment is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה) there, in another place
A saddle or padded cloth placed on a donkey
Is a barrier that blocks the water during immersion
An Italian איסר, a small coin used as a size measure

steps.confusionAlert: 'One side' and 'both sides' means whether the stain stays on one surface of the cloth or soaks through so it shows on both sides. It does not mean two separate stains.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
A grease stain on a saddle is a barrier.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Only when it is as large as an Italian issar.
phrases.notes: A smaller stain is not a barrier

phrases.english: And on clothing,
on one side, it is not a barrier,
on both sides, it is a barrier.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
Even on one side, it is a barrier.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After talking about stains on a תלמיד חכם's clothing, the גמרא brings a משנה about stains in the laws of טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain on a saddle is a barrier. On clothing, the תנא קמא says only a stain on both sides is a barrier, while רבי יהודה says even one side is.

steps.title: Does a saddle need the stain on one side or both?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי חנינא whether the one-side or both-sides rule for clothing also applies to a saddle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש asked רבי חנינא: For a saddle, is a stain on one side enough, or does it need to be on both sides?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks a real question about a detail the משנה left out. The משנה gave the one-side or both-sides rule for clothing, but not for a saddle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says a stain on a saddle is a barrier, without saying how far it must go. Since clothing has a one-side or both-sides rule, ריש לקיש wants to know which standard fits a saddle.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, not an attack)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: מַרְדַּעַת, מִצַּד אֶחָד אוֹ מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין?
phrases.english: A saddle: does it need a stain on one side, or on both sides?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a stain on a saddle is a barrier when it is on one side only, or only when it goes through to both sides.

steps.title: A saddle is no more important than an ignorant person's garment
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא has no direct tradition, but he compares the case to רבי יוסי's ruling. Builders' clothing needs one side, an ignorant person's clothing needs both sides. A saddle is surely no better than the ignorant person's garment, so it needs both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear this, but I heard something like it. We learned that רבי יוסי says: for builders' clothing, one side is enough. For an ignorant person's clothing, it must be on both sides. And a saddle should not be more important than the garment of an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers ריש לקיש by comparing the saddle to a similar case he did hear about. His conclusion is that a saddle needs the stain on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stain only counts as a barrier if the owner cares about it. Careful people (בנאין) care even about a stain on one side, while an עם הארץ only cares when it soaks through. A saddle is treated with even less care than an ignorant person's clothing, so at the very least it needs a stain on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'builders'; explained next as תלמידי חכמים
An ignorant person who is not careful

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a barrier depends on how much the owner cares (מקפיד) is a key principle in the laws of חציצה.

phrases.english: He said to him: This I did not hear,
but I heard something similar to it.
As we learned: Rabbi Yosei says:
Clothing of 'builders': a stain on one side (is a barrier),
and that of an ignorant person: only on both sides.
And a saddle should not be more important
phrases.notes: Said by רבי חנינא as his reasoning

phrases.english: than the garment of an am ha'aretz.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question by comparing it to a similar case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A saddle is like the garment of an עם הארץ (or less), so a stain must be on both sides to be a barrier.

steps.title: Who are the 'builders'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי meant by the word בנאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'builders'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what an unclear word in רבי יוסי's statement means. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real builders are not known for spotless clothing, so a simple reading does not fit. The גמרא wants to know who these careful people are.

phrases.english: What are 'builders'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בַּנָּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the source just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word בנאין in רבי יוסי's statement.

steps.title: The builders are תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'builders' are תלמידי חכמים, who spend their lives building the world through תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: These are תלמידי חכמים, who are busy building the world all their days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question: the 'builders' are Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning תורה keeps the world standing, so scholars are called its builders. This fits the earlier steps, where a תלמיד חכם must keep his clothes clean. That is why he cares even about a stain on one side.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are Torah scholars

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בְּבִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם כׇּל יְמֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: who are busy with building the world all their days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what בנאין means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בנאין are תלמידי חכמים, who build the world through Torah.

steps.title: A scholar trusted to identify his lost item by sight
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the תלמיד חכם who gets back a lost object just by recognizing it is one who is careful to turn his undershirt right side out (if he put it on inside out), so the rough seams do not show.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Which תלמיד חכם do we return a lost object to based on his recognizing it by sight? One who is careful to turn his undershirt the right way, with the seams facing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching from רבי יוחנן about a תלמיד חכם. This one defines which scholar we trust to identify a lost item without giving signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must give specific signs to get back a lost item. A true תלמיד חכם is trusted when he says he recognizes it, since he would not lie. Being careful even about how his clothes look shows he is a refined, real scholar who can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognition by sight, without specific signs

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Which Torah scholar is it
that we return a lost object to him based on recognition by sight?
This is one who is careful to turn his undershirt the right way (seams facing in).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיזֶהוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked by topic: another definition of a תלמיד חכם from the same רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם who is careful even about how his undershirt looks gets back lost items by sight recognition.

steps.title: A scholar fit to lead the community
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a תלמיד חכם may be appointed community leader if he can answer a הלכה question on any topic, even מסכת כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Which תלמיד חכם may be appointed leader over the community? One who is asked a matter of הלכה anywhere and can answer it, even in מסכת כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching of רבי יוחנן: the standard for a scholar to become a community leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leader must be able to answer questions on every topic. מסכת כלה was a little-known tractate, so knowing even that shows complete mastery.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Which Torah scholar is it
that we appoint him leader over the community?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר הֲלָכָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם וְאוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: This is one who is asked a matter of halacha on any topic and answers it,
and even in tractate Kalla.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיזֶהוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמְּמַנִּין אוֹתוֹ פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי יוחנן's definitions of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar who can answer הלכה on every topic, even מסכת כלה, may be appointed community leader.

steps.title: A scholar whose town must help him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the townspeople must do the work of a תלמיד חכם who puts aside his own business to occupy himself with matters of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Which תלמיד חכם must the people of his town do his work for? One who sets aside his own affairs and busies himself with matters of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching of רבי יוחנן: which scholar the town must support by doing his work for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a scholar gives up his own business for Torah and community needs, the community should take care of what he cannot. The next line will limit how far this duty goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Matters of Heaven: Torah and מצוות

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Which Torah scholar is it

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבְּנֵי עִירוֹ מְצֻוִּוין לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ מְלַאכְתּוֹ —
phrases.english: that the people of his town are commanded to do his work for him?
This is one who sets aside his own affairs
and busies himself with matters of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיזֶהוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁבְּנֵי עִירוֹ מְצֻוִּוין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי יוחנן's definitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar who sets aside his own affairs for matters of Heaven must have his work done by his townspeople.

steps.title: The duty is limited to providing his bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי יוחנן's rule: the town only has to make the effort to provide the scholar's food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to making the effort to provide his bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule in the step before. The townspeople must only make sure he has food, not do every kind of work for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Do his work' could sound like the town must do everything for him. The גמרא narrows it to his basic support. They must supply his livelihood so he can keep learning.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to (introduces a limit)
Bread, meaning basic food and support

phrases.english: And this applies only
to making the effort to provide his bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי לְמִיטְרַח בְּרִיפְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the obligation stated in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The town's duty to do the scholar's work is limited to providing his food.

steps.title: The basic definition of a תלמיד חכם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a general definition: a תלמיד חכם is anyone who can answer a הלכה question on whatever topic he is asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Who is a תלמיד חכם? Anyone who is asked a הלכה on any topic and can say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more statement of רבי יוחנן defining a תלמיד חכם in general. This sets up the question of what difference this definition makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds close to the leadership rule in step 17, but here it is a basic definition with no mention of מסכת כלה. The גמרא will next explain its practical use and add levels of appointment.

keyTerms.meaning: And he says it, he can answer it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is just repeating step 17. The next lines show this version leads to two levels: a local leader and a head of ישיבה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Who is a Torah scholar?

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ הֲלָכָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, וְאוֹמְרָהּ.
phrases.english: Anyone who is asked a halacha on any topic, and can state it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיזֶהוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם כׇּל שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another of רבי יוחנן's definitions, close to step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is one who can answer a הלכה on whatever topic he is asked.

steps.title: What practical difference does this definition make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical result comes from defining who is a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this definition matters in practice. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definition should lead to some practical result. The גמרא wants to know what that result is here.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the definition just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of defining someone as a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: Local leader or head of the ישיבה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is for appointing him as a leader. If he knows one tractate, he leads in his own town. If he knows all his learning, he becomes head of the ישיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To appoint him leader over the community. If he knows one tractate, he is appointed in his own place. If he knows all his learning, he is appointed head of the ישיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the definition decides whether, and to what level, a scholar may be appointed leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any topic' is measured by the scope of the position. Someone who has mastered one tractate is fit to lead locally, where questions are limited to that tractate. Someone who has mastered everything he learned may head a ישיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: In his own place or town

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's statements define a תלמיד חכם by different standards for different purposes: care for his clothing (trusted with lost items), full mastery (community leader), dedication to Heaven (town supports him), and level of knowledge (local leader or head of ישיבה).

phrases.english: To appoint him leader over the community.
If (he knows) one tractate, (he is appointed) in his own place;
if (he knows) all of his learning, (he is appointed) head of the yeshiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַנּוֹיֵיהּ פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The definition is for appointing a leader. Mastery of one tractate qualifies him locally, and mastery of all his learning qualifies him to head a ישיבה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש identifies the garments as bath attendants' clothes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different explanation of רבי יוסי's word בנאין: it refers to the clothes of bath attendants from overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: These are the clothes of the bath attendants that come from overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the question from step 14, 'Who are the בנאין?' ריש לקיש gives a different answer from רבי יוחנן: the בנאין in רבי יוסי's statement are bath attendants from overseas, and the garments are their clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the commentators, these are fine clothes on which stains are easily seen, and their wearers are careful to keep them clean. That is why even a stain on one side counts as a barrier. Saying that stains show so easily implies the clothes are white, and the next step attacks exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, an אמורא from ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
These are the clothes of the bath attendants
phrases.notes: Explains the garments mentioned in the משנה.

phrases.english: that come from a country overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of step 14 (מאי בנאין) after the digression of steps 16-22. It gives a different answer from רבי יוחנן's in step 15: the בנאין are overseas bath attendants, not תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The garments in the משנה are the overseas bath attendants' clothes.

steps.title: רבי ינאי's burial request suggests these clothes are red
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether these clothes are white. רבי ינאי asked to be buried in them because they are neither white nor black, which implies they are red.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean these clothes are white? But רבי ינאי told his sons: Do not bury me in white or in black clothes. Not white, in case I am not found worthy and I look like a groom among mourners. Not black, in case I am found worthy and I look like a mourner among grooms. Rather, bury me in the overseas bath attendants' clothes. So these clothes must be red!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. Another source shows that these same clothes are not white at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי chose the bath attendants' clothes because they are neither white nor black. That means they must be a color in between, namely red. If so, how could ריש לקיש's description fit, which made them sound white?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that to say that they are white?
But didn't Rabbi Yannai say to his sons:
My sons, do not bury me

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּכֵלִים לְבָנִים וְלֹא בְּכֵלִים שְׁחוֹרִים,
phrases.english: not in white clothes and not in black clothes.
Not white, in case I am not found worthy in judgment,
and then I will be like a groom among mourners.
Not black, in case I am found worthy,
and then I will be like a mourner among grooms.
Rather, bury me in the clothes of the bath attendants
that come from a country overseas.
This shows that they are red!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּחִיוָּרֵי נִינְהוּ? וְהָאֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's identification of the garments.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea in ריש לקיש's statement that the bath attendants' clothes are white.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי picked these clothes because they are neither white nor black, so they must be red.

steps.title: Outer garments versus inner garments
steps.stepSummary: The red clothes are the outer cloaks, and the white ones are the undergarments.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This source refers to the outer cloaks, and that source refers to the undergarments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both sources are correct, because each one is talking about a different piece of clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bath attendants wore red outer cloaks, which is what רבי ינאי meant. They also wore white undergarments, which is what ריש לקיש meant. So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the outer cloaks,
and that one is about the undergarments.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּגְלִימֵי, הָא בִּלְבוּשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by garment type)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both sources described the same garment, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer cloaks are red (רבי ינאי). The undergarments are white (ריש לקיש).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: שבת fats may be offered on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל's opinion from the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא where he learns from 'עולת שבת בשבתו' that the fats from שבת offerings may be burned on the יום הכיפורים that follows. The reverse is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: One may fold clothes, and so on. רבנן taught: 'The burnt-offering of שבת on its שבת' teaches that the fats of שבת offerings are offered on יום הכיפורים. You might think that the fats of יום הכיפורים offerings may also be offered on שבת. Therefore the פסוק says 'on its שבת.' These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to רבי ישמעאל's statement in the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that shows the source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכיפורים is also called 'שבת,' so 'שבת on its שבת' means a שבת offering may be finished on another 'שבת' that comes right after it. The extra word 'בשבתו' limits this to one direction only. Fats left over from יום הכיפורים may not be burned on the שבת that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats of the offerings brought on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שבת' in the פסוק is read as including יום הכיפורים, which the תורה also calls 'שבת שבתון.' It does not only mean the weekly שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: One may fold, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה, introducing the topic.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat'
teaches about the fats of Shabbat
that they are offered on Yom Kippur.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: One might think that even the fats of Yom Kippur may be offered on Shabbat.
Therefore the verse says: 'on its Shabbat.'
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר מְקַפְּלִין כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי ישמעאל's opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fats from שבת offerings may be burned on the יום הכיפורים that follows. Fats from יום הכיפורים may not be burned on the שבת that follows.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: שבת fats may be offered on יום טוב, not יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the same פסוק to allow the fats of שבת to be offered on a יום טוב that follows. He forbids offering them on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'The burnt-offering of שבת on its שבת' teaches that the fats of שבת are offered on יום טוב. You might think they may be offered even on יום הכיפורים. Therefore the פסוק says 'on its שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about what the same פסוק teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the פסוק allows burning שבת fats on a יום טוב that follows. The word 'בשבתו' excludes יום הכיפורים. This is the exact opposite of רבי ישמעאל, who used the פסוק to allow יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading תנא who argues with רבי ישמעאל here
On its own שבת (the limiting word)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat'
teaches about the fats of Shabbat
that they are offered on a Festival.
One might think they may be offered even on Yom Kippur.
Therefore the verse says: 'on its Shabbat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: עוֹלַת שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fats from שבת offerings may be burned on the יום טוב that follows, but not on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the root of the dispute. רבי ישמעאל holds that נדרים ונדבות may be brought on יום טוב, so the פסוק is needed only for יום הכיפורים. רבי עקיבא holds they may not be brought on יום טוב, so the פסוק is needed to permit יום טוב. The section closes by introducing a statement of רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you look into it, you will find this. According to רבי ישמעאל, vow and free-will offerings are brought on יום טוב, so the verse is needed for יום הכיפורים. According to רבי עקיבא, vow and free-will offerings are not brought on יום טוב, so the verse is needed to permit יום טוב. רבי זירא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא read the פסוק so differently. At the very end, the גמרא sets up a new statement by רבי זירא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל already allows even optional offerings on יום טוב. So leftover שבת fats on יום טוב are obviously allowed, and the פסוק must be teaching something new: יום הכיפורים. רבי עקיבא forbids optional offerings on יום טוב, so he needs the פסוק to permit שבת fats on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: When you look into it, you will find
Vow offerings and free-will offerings (optional sacrifices)

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא uses the פסוק to teach whatever would not be allowed without it. For רבי ישמעאל, that is יום הכיפורים. For רבי עקיבא, that is יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the dispute over the פסוק really depends on a deeper disagreement: whether optional offerings may be brought on יום טוב.

phrases.english: When you look into it, you will find:
According to Rabbi Yishmael,
vow and free-will offerings are offered on a Festival,
